title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 235 (Power to acquire shares of shareholders dissenting from scheme or contract approved by majority)

content.overview: Section 235 provides that where a scheme or contract involving the transfer of shares or any class of shares in a company to another company has been approved by the holders of not less than nine-tenths in value of the shares whose transfer is involved (other than shares already held by the transferee or its nominee/subsidiary) within the prescribed time, the transferee company may give notice to the dissenting shareholders to acquire their shares. A dissentient may apply to the Tribunal. If no order is made against the acquisition, the transferee is bound and entitled to acquire on the terms of the scheme. This is the statutory squeeze-out route; section 236 is the separate minority-purchase route at the 90% holding threshold.
content.glance: Scheme/contract for share transfer approved by ≥9/10 in value within time → transferee may notice dissentients to acquire; dissentient may apply to Tribunal; if no adverse order, acquire on scheme terms; squeeze-out route (distinct from s. 236).
content.study: Where a scheme or contract involving the transfer of shares or any class of shares in a company to another company has, within the time prescribed, been approved by the holders of not less than nine-tenths in value of the shares whose transfer is involved (other than shares already held at the date of the offer by the transferee or its nominee or subsidiary), the transferee company may give notice to any dissenting shareholder that it desires to acquire his shares. Current-law framing: confirm scheme/contract for transfer of shares; achieve nine-tenths in value approval within time (excluding shares already held by transferee side); serve notice on dissentients; dissentient may apply to Tribunal; absent an order against acquisition, transferee acquires on scheme terms. Distinguish s. 236 (acquirer already holding 90%+ notifies to buy remaining equity).

sections.heading: Threshold
sections.body: Scheme or contract for transfer of shares approved by holders of not less than nine-tenths in value within the prescribed time (excluding shares already held by transferee/nominee/subsidiary).

sections.heading: Notice
sections.body: Transferee may give notice to dissenting shareholders to acquire their shares.

sections.heading: Tribunal Application
sections.body: Dissentient may apply to the Tribunal; if no order is made against the acquisition, transferee is bound and entitled to acquire on the scheme terms.

sections.heading: Relationship to s. 236
sections.body: s. 235 is the squeeze-out on a scheme/contract with 9/10 approval; s. 236 is purchase of minority where acquirer already holds 90%+ of issued equity.

provisions.title: Power to acquire shares of shareholders dissenting from scheme or contract approved by majority

examples.title: Squeeze-out after 9/10 approval
examples.body: A takeover scheme is approved by holders of 92% in value of the shares to be transferred within the prescribed time. The transferee serves notice under s. 235 on the remaining dissentients to acquire their shares on the scheme terms.

examples.title: Dissentient applies to Tribunal
examples.body: A dissentient challenges the acquisition notice under s. 235 before the Tribunal. If the Tribunal makes no order against the acquisition, the transferee is entitled and bound to acquire on the scheme terms.

hypotheticals.question: Is s. 235 available without any scheme or contract for transfer of shares?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 235 is triggered by a scheme or contract involving the transfer of shares that has been approved by nine-tenths in value. It is not a free-standing buyout power independent of such a scheme or contract.

distinctions.title: Squeeze-out of dissentients (s. 235) vs purchase of minority (s. 236)
distinctions.left: Scheme/contract approved by 9/10 in value; notice to acquire dissentients
distinctions.right: Acquirer already holds 90%+ of issued equity; notify company; minority may also require buy

misconceptions.trap: Any majority shareholder can force out the minority under s. 235 without a scheme.
misconceptions.correction: Section 235 requires a scheme or contract for transfer of shares approved by nine-tenths in value within the prescribed time. It is not a general majority buyout power.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 235 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm scheme/contract and 9/10 approval within time. II. Notice to dissentients. III. Tribunal application path. IV. Distinguish s. 236. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Scheme; value approval; notice; Tribunal issues; precise relief.

enhancement.definition: Section 235 allows a transferee, after a scheme or contract for share transfer is approved by nine-tenths in value within time, to give notice to acquire dissenting shares, subject to the dissentient’s right to apply to the Tribunal.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Once a qualifying majority accepts a share-transfer scheme, the law permits compulsory acquisition of dissentients on the same terms, subject to Tribunal oversight.
essentialIngredients: Scheme or contract for transfer of shares
Approval by ≥9/10 in value within prescribed time
Dissentient may apply to Tribunal; acquisition on scheme terms if no adverse order
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 235 is the classic statutory squeeze-out following a majority-approved share scheme.
enhancement.problemApplication: Confirm scheme and threshold; serve notice; address Tribunal path.
